title.narrative: Promoting Female Sanitation and Hygiene Awareness Through Radio Programs

description.narrative: The project aims to promote female sanitation and hygiene awareness in high schools in Liberia through radio programs. This initiative recognizes the importance of promoting good hygiene practices among young girls to improve their overall health and well-being. By utilizing radio programs, the project intends to reach a wide audience of high school students and educate them on proper sanitation and hygiene practices specifically tailored to the needs of adolescent girls. The content of the radio programs will cover topics such as menstrual hygiene management, hand washing, access to clean water, and the importance of maintaining good personal hygiene. Through engaging and informative radio broadcasts, the project seeks to empower young girls with the knowledge and skills necessary to adopt healthy hygiene habits that will promote their well-being. The project aims to address the critical issue of female sanitation and hygiene awareness in Liberia through targeted radio programs. Liberia faces challenges in promoting proper hygiene practices among females, leading to health issues according to the World Health Organization (WHO), United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), and Liberia Ministry of Education give their expertise on public health, child welfare, and educational policies related to sanitation, hygiene, and adolescent health in Liberia. This project seeks to leverage the influential medium of radio to disseminate essential information and foster behavioral change regarding female sanitation and hygiene. However, the lack of adequate information on sanitation and hygiene practices among females poses significant health risks among young females in Liberia. In response, this project proposes the development and implementation of radio programs aimed at raising awareness and promoting better sanitation and hygiene practices among high school female students in Liberia.
